## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`--exclude` needs to take its default from an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment variable. The project's CLI flag policy requires this for every new flag under `cli/`, so CI cannot set the option until it is added.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag. `collect` uses `fnmatch` to skip files whose base name matches any of the patterns. The pull request also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds unit and end-to-end tests, and adds a one-line test fixture.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Default --exclude from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — When CI sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, nothing excludes files, because `--exclude` uses `default=[]` and never reads the environment. This breaks `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable … because CI sets options through the environment." — CI jobs that set options through the environment cannot exclude files, so excluded files still end up in their archives. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")` using a separator you document in `docs/flags.md:7`, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` to cover the variable both set and unset.
